promise: Every `hangar --json` run that reaches the fleet prints a valid JSON document: the matching hosts, or `[]` when nothing matched and when there is no cache yet. Each host carries its own tags.
why: A query that simply matched no host printed nothing at all, so `jq` downstream failed on empty input for an answer rather than an error, and so did a machine with no cache yet, which is where a first pipeline is likeliest to run. The document also dropped the instance's tags, which made 'everything in the payments ASG' unanswerable from a cache that holds it. Runs the built binary against a fixture cache rather than grepping, because mistake 16 was an eval that could not fail. The promise is scoped to runs that reach the fleet: a usage error prints nothing on stdout on purpose, because the command never ran. The tag it asserts on is one no mapping lists as a candidate, so the case does not depend on whose config.json ran it.
command: bin=app/.build/debug/hangar-cli; swift build --package-path app --product hangar-cli >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1; tmp=$(mktemp -d) || exit 1; printf '%s' '{"instances": [{"id": "i-0123456789abcdef0", "state": "running", "type": "t3.small", "launchTime": "2026-08-20T15:46:42.000Z", "tags": {"product": "payments", "env": "prod", "Name": "web", "hangar-eval-marker": "kept"}}], "region": "us-west-2", "fetchedAt": 800000000}' > "$tmp/cache"; empty=$("$bin" --cache "$tmp/cache" --json zzzznosuchhostanywhere 2>/dev/null); full=$("$bin" --cache "$tmp/cache" --json 2>/dev/null); nocache=$("$bin" --cache "$tmp/absent" --json 2>/dev/null); rm -rf "$tmp"; printf '%s' "$empty" | /usr/bin/python3 -c 'import json,sys; sys.exit(0 if json.load(sys.stdin)==[] else 1)' || exit 1; printf '%s' "$nocache" | /usr/bin/python3 -c 'import json,sys; sys.exit(0 if json.load(sys.stdin)==[] else 1)' || exit 1; printf '%s' "$full" | /usr/bin/python3 -c 'import json,sys; r=json.load(sys.stdin)[0]; sys.exit(0 if r["tags"]["hangar-eval-marker"]=="kept" and "type" in r and "launch_time" in r else 1)'
